Welcome to Oakley Church of England Junior School
Great expectations for all through Courage, Respect and Grace.
Our vision at Oakley is to create great expectations for all, using our Christian values and the teachings of Jesus to allow our children and community to flourish.
It is my pleasure to welcome you to Oakley Church of England Junior School.
Our school thrives on a foundation of 'Great Expectations for All'. Whatever their starting point, circumstances or needs, we have unfailingly high expectations of each and every child in our care.
Our core Christian values of Courage, Respect and Grace guide us in achieving these great expectations. Please see further information about our Christian values here:
As a voluntary controlled Church of England Junior School, we have strong links with our local church-St Leonard's and our pupils take an active role in supporting the local community.
The intent of our broad and balanced curriculum is rooted in our core Christian values:
With courage, our pupils are encouraged to always do their best and not give in to discouragement. They are also guided to stand by what is right and true in considering aspects of morality in the different topics.
Through respect, our curriculum celebrates difference and allows every child to demonstrate their strengths and make good progress. Our pupils should be able to see themselves and their diversity within our curriculum.
Grace is shown through the active kindness and generosity of collaborative learning. We also encourage our pupils to demonstrate grace outside of our school in our local community and the wider world.
Our pupils’ spirituality is developed through collective worship and moments of spiritual awareness throughout the curriculum.
The social, emotional, physical and mental health and wellbeing of our pupils is the foundation from which they will thrive. We pride ourselves on the wide variety of provisions we have at Oakley CE Junior School to develop the social, emotional, physical and mental health and wellbeing of all our pupils.
Sarah Hill - Headteacher
If you would like to visit the school to find out more, please contact the school office by either telephone 01256 780433 or email.

After School Clubs and Wrap Around Care
After school clubs organised by the school for the Autmn Term will resume on Thursday 4th Spetember 2025 and can now be booked online and are payable in advance.
After school clubs and wrap around care run by ActiveMe360 need to be booked via their website.
You will see any after school club run by the school on your SCOPay account by Tuesday 22nd July. This also means that your child has been allocated a space. You will only be contacted if the club is full or if the club is no longer offered due to low numbers.
Where there are limits to numbers, we will take bookings on a first-come-first-served basis and we will operate a waiting list. Should this club be run at another time in the year, children who missed out will be offered places first. Where there is spare capacity within a club, we may open it up to other year groups.
Where a teacher is away or on a course, we will do everything we can to run the club with another teacher. Where a club is cancelled by us, the amount for this session can be either refunded at the school office or held as a credit on your child's SCOPay dinner account.
If your child is in receipt of free school meals, one club that is run by the school will be available free of charge.
Please collect your child promptly when the club / wrap-around care finishes. We accept that on occasion you may run into difficulties. Please let us know at the earliest opportunity. If for any reason, your chld is not collected on time (at 4.30pm) after one of the Junior School after-school clubs, a member of staff will endeavour to make contact with you. A member of staff will wait with your child in the reception area until 4.45pm. If your child has not been collected after this time, the same member of staff will accompany your child over to Oakley Infant School where they will join the ActiveMe360 after-school club which runs until 6.00pm. If your child is taken to the ActiveMe360 club, this will incur a charge.
Although we don’t anticipate any difficulties, we do reserve the right to exclude any child whose behaviour we deem inappropriate, unsafe or unacceptable. We want everyone to enjoy their club experience.

PE and Sport Premium
At Oakley Church of England School, we recognise the contribution of PE to the health and well-being of the children. We believe that an innovative, varied PE curriculum and extra-curricular opportunities have a positive influence on the concentration, attitude and academic achievement of all our children. Our Primary School Sport’s Funding will enable us to continue and extend our provision through employing additional sports professionals, entering into more competitive sports competitions and training our staff to deliver in-house quality PE sessions.
Visit https://www.gov.uk/guidance/pe-and-sport-premium-for-primary-schools for the Department of Education Primary School’s Sports Funding page.
The government is providing funding to provide new and substantial primary school sport funding. The funding is being jointly provided by the Departments for Education, Health and Culture, Media and Sport, and will see money going directly to primary school headteachers to spend on improving the quality of sport and PE for all their children. The money can only be spent on sport and PE provision in schools.
Schools will have to spend the sport funding on improving their provision of PE and sport, but they will have the freedom to choose how they do this.
